backup.sundayFailed.title: Backup failed: Sunday's snapshot wasn't added to the sync folder
backup.sundayFailed.body: The snapshot from {date} (Sunday) didn't make it into the sync folder at the time, and this retry failed too: {reason}.
backup.localFailed.title: Backup failed: couldn't take the local snapshot
backup.localFailed.body: The backup at {when} failed: {reason}. The sync folder wasn't updated either.
backup.syncFailed.title: Backup failed: couldn't write to the sync folder
backup.syncFailed.body: Backup at {when}: the local snapshot is done ({date} in the local backup area), but it wasn't written to the sync folder: {reason}.
backup.checkFailed.title: Snapshot check failed: {date} in {place}
backup.checkFailed.body: Check: the latest snapshot in {place} ({date}) failed the integrity check: {problems}{more}. The next backup will take a fresh snapshot; avoid this one if you need to restore.
backup.syncDir.placeholder: The sync folder in the config is still the example placeholder ({dir}); change it to a real sync folder on this computer
backup.owner.unknown: unknown owner (the lock file isn't fully written yet)
backup.busy: another backup ({owner}) still hadn't finished after 2 hours, so this one was skipped
backup.overdue.body_one: Backups are left to an external timer (backup.schedule is external). The last one was at {last}, and nothing has run for {n} day since. Check whether the scheduled task that runs {command} every day was paused or deleted, or tap “Back up now” to take one right away.
backup.overdue.body_other: Backups are left to an external timer (backup.schedule is external). The last one was at {last}, and nothing has run for {n} days since. Check whether the scheduled task that runs {command} every day was paused or deleted, or tap “Back up now” to take one right away.
backup.overdue.neverBody_one: Backups are left to an external timer (backup.schedule is external), and none has run in the {n} day since {since}. Check that the scheduled task that runs {command} every day exists and isn't paused, or tap “Back up now” to take one right away.
backup.overdue.neverBody_other: Backups are left to an external timer (backup.schedule is external), and none has run in the {n} days since {since}. Check that the scheduled task that runs {command} every day exists and isn't paused, or tap “Back up now” to take one right away.
backup.config.unreadable: Couldn't read the config file {file} ({reason}); nothing changed
backup.config.notUtf8: The config file {file} isn't UTF-8; nothing changed, so its text doesn't get damaged
backup.config.notJson: The config file {file} isn't valid JSON right now ({reason}); nothing changed. Fix it first
backup.config.notObject: The top level of the config file {file} isn't an object; nothing changed. Fix it first
backup.config.sectionNotObject: backup in the config file {file} isn't an object; nothing changed. Fix it first
backup.config.invalid: The backup section of the config file is wrong; nothing changed: {reason}
backup.config.editFailed: Editing the config file {file} failed its check; nothing written
backup.config.badTime: The time must look like HH:mm (for example 03:30), got {time}
backup.folder.empty: Give the full path of a folder
backup.folder.placeholder: {dir} is still the placeholder from the sample; use a real folder on this computer
backup.folder.notAbsolute: Use a full path (for example D:\NAS\ergo-backup); {dir} isn't one
backup.folder.insideData: {dir} is inside the data folder ({dataDir}), so it would be lost together with the data. Pick a folder outside it
backup.open.noSync: No sync folder is set yet
backup.restore.setDataDir: First set the data folder (yours isn't the default one; run the next commands in the same window)
backup.restore.stop: Stop ergo first (restoring requires it to be stopped)
backup.restore.one: Restore a given day (change the date to the one you want)
backup.restore.fromSync: If the local copy is damaged: restore from the sync folder
backup.restore.start: Start ergo again when it's done
